recognize_zh: 箭頭所指的紅血球比周圍的大、顏色偏灰藍、沒有中央淡染區，這就是多染性紅血球（polychromatophilic cells，對應網狀紅血球）。
features: Scattered large red cells (arrows) with bluish-gray (polychromatophilic) cytoplasm and no central pallor
Polychromatophilic cells are larger than surrounding normocytic red cells
Background red cells show mild anisopoikilocytosis with occasional teardrop and elongated forms
Occasional small red cells with reduced central pallor, possible spherocytes
Platelets present; no nucleated red cells or red cell inclusions in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows red cells with mild anisopoikilocytosis. Several larger red cells with bluish-gray cytoplasm and absent central pallor (polychromatophilic cells) are highlighted by arrows, indicating increased reticulocytes. Occasional small red cells with reduced central pallor are present and may represent spherocytes; no nucleated red cells, schistocytes, or inclusions are identified in this field. Findings are consistent with polychromasia reflecting a marrow regenerative response, as seen in hemolytic anemia.

ddx.vs: Macrocytes and oval macrocytes are large but retain normal pink hemoglobin color without a blue-gray RNA tint.
Spherocytes are small, dense, and hyperchromatic without central pallor, whereas polychromatophilic cells are large and paler blue-gray.

Artifactual bluish tint affects cells diffusely in thick areas, whereas true polychromasia involves individual larger cells scattered among normally stained cells and correlates with a raised reticulocyte count.
